scope: Two runtime repairs, owned regressions/full API checks and a fresh single-policy hundred-target measurement. Chromium remains default; hosted parity is unproven.

changes.blobResources: For non-navigation blob resources with an HTTP/HTTPS origin, run the same private-destination and ad policy against that origin, then continue browser-local resolution. Top-level blob URLs/navigation, opaque/file origins and private origins remain blocked. Worker network requests retain route/proxy and UID network controls.
changes.navigationEof: Only the exact WebKit page.goto connection-termination first line becomes NETWORK_ERROR / WEBKIT_CONNECTION_TERMINATED. Existing explicit retry and bounded distinct-engine fallback can use it after closure proof. Certificate rejection, other TLS failures, crashes and evaluation errors stay outside this mapping.
changes.apiContract: Existing owner discovery and closed-attempt handling needed no API runtime change. Three new full API snips exercise actual blob rendering, navigation termination/Firefox recovery and failure boundaries.

pacing.limit: Slot reservation precedes fetch. Observed gaps are retained; configuration is not an exact dispatch floor.

fullApiBenchmark.comparisonLimit: Single-policy fresh run after two repairs, not a contemporaneous paired old-code or hosted comparison. No new primary-only score is inferred from fallback responses. The historical 46 primary/56 fallback and hosted82 observations remain separately dated evidence.

comparisonWithPreviousWebkitPolicy.limit: Same frozen targets and configured policy/resources, different live epoch. Each policy visits each target once; not an interleaved randomized old-code/new-code comparison.

observedBackendBehavior.limit: Returned API receipts carry errorCode but do not preserve every primary engine network alias/document diagnostic. Log counts and returned receipts are distinct evidence; no unrecorded per-target causal attribution.

nativeFocusedHelpers.scope: Transport typing, cancellation/deadlines, URL-origin policy, private destinations and pinned DNS. Repository test-force-exit option retained; an earlier invocation used the wrong working directory and was corrected.

ownedBeforeAfter.fixtureCaveat: The first transport fixture required HTTP/2 and failed at ALPN before a request. It was corrected to accept HTTP/1.1/HTTP2 before the real navigation-EOF regression. The phrase does not establish a remote target protocol. Earlier fixture/debug receipts are retained, not counted as proof of EOF reproduction.

fullApiSnips.command: pnpm harness pnpm exec vitest run src/__tests__/snips/v2/browser-webkit-recovery.test.ts
negativeCases: Certificate rejection reaches neither HTTP fixture handler nor alternate.
fullApiSnips.teardownLimit: Harness returned0 and terminated processes; extract-worker again logged Channel closing during teardown. This is not clean worker-shutdown evidence.
fullApiSnips.ownedEofTlsException: The owned self-signed fixture uses an explicit TLS-verification exception only for the EOF positive path. The negative case enables verification and is rejected; public benchmark requests retain verification.

remainingWork: Investigate the separately observed renderer crash and non-proper TLS termination with owned faults before adding any new fallback eligibility.
Preserve primary network aliases/document diagnostics through returned API fallback receipts so future per-target recovery attribution is direct.
Keep the frozen grading unchanged and distinguish aggregate live variance from owned-regression correctness; no new hosted calls were made.

research.finding: Blob URLs reference a browser store and have origin/partition restrictions; they are not themselves arbitrary outbound HTTP connections.

The upstream HTTP2 EOF path uses the observed termination phrase. Owned tests also reproduced navigation termination while accepting HTTP1; wording alone does not prove a failing public target used HTTP2.

selection.rule: GitHub/arxiv controls, first eight old/new full-run disagreements in the frozen target order; if fewer than eight, fill from the stated prior-failure list. This is a selected diagnostic cohort, not population coverage.

matchedDiagnosticComparison.scope: Matched previous/repaired WebKit browser-service comparison on ten selected targets, including two controls. Both headful Linux ARM64 owners use the production UID policy, 2 CPU/2 GiB and one page. Two workers, alternating dispatch order, fresh contexts and no retries/proxies/hints/hosted calls. Direct service deadlines are 30 seconds, not the full API deadline; results cannot be added to the hundred-target API score.
matchedDiagnosticComparison.comparisonLimit: Ten selected WebKit browser-service targets, one visit per variant, not a new full API score, Firefox fallback comparison or a powered causal test. Different transport state, live epoch and target-rate effects remain. Both variants use the same configured resources and request controls.

requestAccounting.limits: The extra ten-target comparison is reported separately and is not added to the hundred-target API score. Research fetches/geolocation probes are ancillary, not benchmark target captures.
